name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Check that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: semantic-crosscheck generates a PostgreSQL 17 hierarchy closure, SQL and SHACL data rules, an OWL ontology and a Cube data model from one crosscheck.toml, then checks on your data that they agree with each other and with hand-written gold SQL. Optional stages cover literal expected-row fixtures (expect), dual SQL/Python data-rules evaluation, synthetic counterexamples, grain and preflight contracts, and offline PostgreSQL 17 SQL structure checks. A pass means the checks that ran found no disagreement on this snapshot; it is not proof that the model or the business rules are right, and not_proven lines disclose empty comparisons, generated-only mutant kills, and unchecked facets or runtimes. The report shows which evidence covers each measure facet. An optional raw-row oracle checks grouping, time windows and join fan-out. Results hold counts, check IDs and digests only, never row values or credentials (v0.34.0).
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
